direction_notes: Central thalamic sonication slowed responses and increased lapses on the PVT and reduced target detection on the EDT, consistent with reduced arousal; pulvinar sonication produced more subtle contralateral visuospatial attention deficits.
safety_notes: The paper states the intensities comply with FDA diagnostic ultrasound guidelines and have no known adverse thermal bioeffects; no adverse event reporting is given.

device.model: BXPulsar 1002 drive system with fixed-focal-length single-element spherical transducer (80 mm focal length, 61 mm aperture)

timing.protocol_description: Ultrasound was delivered in an on/off block design including 10 blocks with 30 seconds of sonication and 30 seconds of rest (30 s pulse train duration; 0.5 ms pulse duration, 100 Hz PRF, 5% duty cycle). Tasks (PVT and EDT) were run before and after sonication in each session; sessions at least 24 hours apart.

source_quotes.n_subjects: In a within-subjects, counterbalanced design, 27 healthy volunteers completed the Psychomotor Vigilance Task (PVT), a vigilance task, and the Egly-Driver Task (EDT), which assesses visuospatial attention, before and after central thalamus, pulvinar, and sham sonication with tFUS.
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: Participants underwent an MRI scan followed by three sonication sessions, including one per ultrasound condition: sham, pulvinar, and central thalamus sonication.
source_quotes.exposures[0].in_situ.isppa_w_cm2: Ultrasound was delivered in an on/off block design including 10 blocks with 30 seconds of sonication and 30 seconds of rest. We used a 0.5 ms pulse duration (PD), 60 s pulse repetition interval (PRI), 5% duty cycle (DC), 100 Hz pulse repetition frequency (PRF), < 720 mW/cm<sup>2</sup> I<sub>spta.3</sub>, and < 14.40 W/cm<sup>2</sup> I<sub>sppa.3</sub> based on previous work [53]. These intensities comply with the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) guidelines for diagnostic ultrasound [94] and have no known adverse thermal bioeffects [95, 96]. This regime was selected because previous work demonstrates that it has suppressive effects when applied to the thalamus [53].

flags.reason: Methods text gives a 60 s pulse repetition interval while the Figure 1 legend gives a 10 ms PRI (100 Hz PRF); recorded the stated 100 Hz PRF and 5% duty cycle.

Intensities are labelled Ispta.3 / Isppa.3 (derated notation) but the paper does not say whether they are free-field or in situ; placed in unspecified_domain. Given as upper bounds (<=720 mW/cm2, <=14.40 W/cm2). Methods write '<' and the legend writes '<='.
Same intensity statement applies to both targets; domain not stated.
Central thalamus 'includes the intralaminar thalamic nuclei and adjacent areas'; mapped to generic thalamus.
Behavioural impairment after central thalamic sonication; authors suggest this is consistent with suppression but no neural readout was recorded.
Only participants stated to be blinded; experimenter blinding not stated.
